data.body:
OPERATOR-ATTESTED EVIDENCE — Bedrock invokability probe (S6 Step 1).

Executed from this environment against the account named in the ticket. Two calls, both exit 0.

1. Model availability — `aws bedrock list-foundation-models --region us-east-1`, filtered to claude:
     anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0
     anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0
     anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
     anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1
     anthropic.claude-opus-5
     anthropic.claude-fable-5

2. INVOKABILITY (the probe the AC asks for) — `aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model`:
     region    us-east-1
     model-id  us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0
     request   max_tokens 16, one user message
     RESPONSE  model=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001  text='ok'
               usage={'input_tokens': 14, 'output_tokens': 4,
                      'cache_creation_input_tokens': 0, 'cache_read_input_tokens': 0}

Caller identity: arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier — the account 896586841071 named in the
criterion. So Bedrock is reachable AND invokable from this environment; S6/S8 are not blocked on
credentials.

NOTE ON METHOD, so this is reproducible: AWS CLI v2 requires `--cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out`
for a JSON --body. Without it the call fails with 'Invalid base64' — which looks like an access error
but is a client-side encoding error. A first attempt here failed that way and was NOT an access
failure.

This attests Step 1 only. The paired-run ParityReport (the ticket's other operator-attested criterion)
still needs a real side-by-side run and is not covered by this comment.
